newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to raise domestic liquor taxes - reports.
newsitem.headline: Japan to raise domestic liquor taxes - reports.

text.p: Japan's Finance Ministry is likely to raise taxes on domestic liquor while cutting those for foreign liquor such as whiskey, following a World Trade Organisation ruling that its tax system treats foreign spirits unfairly, Japanese newspaper reports said on Wednesday.
Finance ministry officials in charge of the issue were not immediately available for comment.

Media reports said that the ministry is negotiating with the ruling Liberal Democratic Party to raise taxes on shochu, a popular domestic liquor made from materials such as barley, to around 12 yen per degree of alcohol, which would be about two to three times its current rate. At the same time, it plans to lower the tax on whiskey to about half of its current rate of 24.56 yen per degree of alcohol, the reports said.

Although the ministry wants to start implementing the measures gradually over a span of three to five years, European countries want the measures to be introduced from the next fiscal year starting on April 1, 1997, the reports said.
The World Trade Organisation, ruling on a complaint by the European Union, the United States and Canada, recently found that Japan taxes imported spirits unfairly compared to domestic liquor.

Japan told the WTO's Dispute Settlement Body last month that it would make its laws conform to the finding, but that it would need time to shape the necessary measures. Under WTO rules, Japan has approximately 15 months to comply.
